reading.body:
T5 Charlotte Campus in Kings Mountain publishes no power consumption figure. The operator describes an on-site Duke Energy substation and a location 30 miles from Charlotte Douglas International Airport, but has not disclosed IT load, total campus power, PUE, cooling capacity, or rack count on its dedicated campus page. Without published specifications, the campus cannot be assessed against other facilities or interpreted for AI scaling capacity.

North Carolina has 19 mapped data center facilities, of which 5 publish power figures totaling 50.3 MW. This campus ranks sixth among published North Carolina capacity but contributes zero to the state total because it publishes no megawatt figure. Whether T5 Charlotte represents significant uncommitted power available to AI workloads remains unknown from public sources.

The absence of published specifications is itself notable. Many newer and retrofit facilities built for GPU-intensive AI training disclose power budgets and PUE as competitive facts. A substation-equipped campus with an address and operator attribution but no power disclosure suggests either early-stage buildout, non-AI customer commitments, or a operator choice not to publish. None of these facts determine the campus's relevance to AI infrastructure, but they mean it cannot yet be read from available data.
